headline: LG Electronics has signed a long-term deal, which it values at several billion dollars, to supply cooling equipment for AI data centers in North America.
score_reason: Pool 6 kept: a signed, jointly announced supply deal of stated size; the dollar value is LG's own estimate.
importance_line: Builders and operators of AI data centers gain a large, long-term supply of cooling equipment at a time when heat limits how fast new capacity can be built, but the value is LG's own estimate and delivery is phased with no schedule given.
summary: Korea JoongAng Daily reports that LG Electronics' US arm has signed a long-term agreement with AIR Control Concepts, a company that designs and builds data centers in the US and Canada, to supply chillers (large machines that cool water to carry heat out of a building) and other cooling equipment, in phases, for AI data centers totaling about 5 gigawatts of capacity (a gigawatt is a billion watts, roughly one large power plant). The contract value was not disclosed, but an LG spokesperson said it was worth several trillion won, or several billion dollars, and the report calls cooling one of the main limits on building AI data centers because AI chips give off far more heat than ordinary servers.
notes: Cross-checked with the joint LG and AIR release on PR Newswire dated 5 Oct 2026, which says more than 5GW and spells the partner AIR Control Concepts. The dollar value is only an LG spokesperson's statement to Korea JoongAng Daily. Earlier LG cooling items in our 27 Sep and 1 Oct 2026 editions were different news (Nvidia network, Virginia chiller factory).
